title: BORN2FLAP — Ornithopter Flight Simulator
meta_desc: BORN2FLAP is a real-time ornithopter flight simulator: segmented wings, dynamic stall and aeroelastic bending. Every wingbeat counts.
hero_greeting: Fly the machine. Become the wing.
hero_lead: A real-time ornithopter simulator built on a reduced physics core — segmented wings, partial stall, spanwise crossflow, aeroelastic bending. No hidden stability tricks. Every force is earned by the wing.
hero_version: ALPHA 1 · Free & Open Source · Unreal Engine 5 · Haskell MathCore
essence_lead: An ornithopter is not a quad. It is a beating wing.
essence_body: Where a drone hovers by force of motors, an ornithopter is the air it pushes. BORN2FLAP models the wing — its geometry, its stiffness, its camber, its stall — and lets the machine find flight on its own. Thrust, lift and control all emerge from one source: the wingbeat.
essence_p1_body: Segmented wings, partial stall, added mass and aeroelastic bending — resolved at a fixed timestep, never faked.
essence_p2_body: CRSF radio, ONDAS mixers, PID and servo kernels ported from real firmware. Fly it with a real transmitter.
essence_p3_body: Sweep, washout, camber and stiffness change how it flies. Build it, then survive it.
flight_body: Two wings, sixteen spanwise strips each. Local angle of attack, Reynolds number and separation state are computed per strip. Crossflow drifts along the span with sweep. The wing bends under load — torsional washout softens the tip, bending deepens the flap — and that deformation feeds straight back into incidence.
arch_haskell_desc: The canonical physics — aerodynamics, kinematics, control and stabilisation. Pure, total, tested.
arch_unreal_desc: Rendering, Chaos rigid bodies, world interaction, cockpit, replay and game modes.
arch_bridge_desc: The FFI boundary into Unreal, plus the tested OrniCore research fallback.
arch_ruby_desc: App state, menus, rules and orchestration — the slow mind behind the fast math.
arch_pipeline:

game_lead: Light to begin, hard to master.
game_free_desc: Open skies, thermal hunting, and the pure pleasure of staying aloft.
game_school_desc: Nine lessons from neutral trim to manual tuning — ghost sticks, corridors, replays.
game_race_desc: Gates, splits, ghosts and classes through canyons and cities.
game_freestyle_desc: Trick challenges judged by the wing, not the scoreboard.
game_landing_desc: Spot landings in wind — the oldest discipline, the hardest.
game_bench_desc: Wind-tunnel view: force vectors, stall maps, live wing deformation.
open_body: BORN2FLAP ships on Steam and the Epic Games Store, and its own source is released under the MIT license. The physics core, the bridge, the brain — open. Fly the game, then take the wing and build your own. Unreal Engine and third-party assets keep their own licenses.
footer_hermetic: Written in the æther by ferocious hearts.
doc_lead: The wing, the math, and the machine — explained.
ph_markdown:
The simulation resolves a full vehicle at a **fixed 240 Hz** timestep: two wings, a body, and a tail.

## Reference frames

- **Body** — +x forward, +y right, +z up (Unreal's left-handed layout).
- **Wing local** — x chordwise toward the trailing edge, y root→tip, z wing normal.

All units are SI internally; the Unreal boundary converts metres ↔ centimetres.

## Discretisation

- 16 spanwise strips per wing (Haskell simulates both wings; C++ OrniCore simulates one isolated wing as the research reference).
- Local angle of attack, Reynolds number and separation state are computed **per strip**.

## Forces

- **Lift** — perpendicular to the local planar flow.
- **Drag** — opposes the local planar flow; dissipative.
- **Separation** — a continuous per-element state from 0 (attached) to 1 (separated), giving partial stall.
- **Added mass** — the reaction of the air the wing accelerates.
- **LEV** — leading-edge vortex lift captured in the stall model.
- **Crossflow** — spanwise transport driven by sweep, gated by flapping phase.

Signs and constants are single-sourced in `docs/physics-convention.md` and asserted by regression tests.
wing_markdown:
Wing geometry is a **single source of truth** — an arbitrary outline, not bird-specific scalars.

## Planform

A `WingShape` is a half-span plus an ordered list of spanwise stations. Each station carries leading-edge position, chord, twist and dihedral. **Sweep is implicit** — the slope of the leading-edge polyline — never a stored parameter.

## Section

Every station carries a `SectionProfile`: rest camber, trailing-edge reflex, and membrane compliance. The thin-airfoil response shifts the zero-lift angle with camber and couples camber + reflex into a sectional pitching moment.

## Structure

Every station carries a `StructureProfile`: bending stiffness **EI**, torsional stiffness **GJ**, and relaxation times. A root-clamped cantilever pass turns vertical force into bending moment → deflection/slope, and sectional pitching moment into torque → twist. A stiffer armwing and a flexible handwing yield realistic load-induced washout.

## Aeroelastic loop

Deformation is not cosmetic. Aeroelastic twist adds to incidence; bending adds to flap position. The wing feeds its own loads back into its shape — the beating wing is a structure, not a picture.
wave_markdown:
The flapping waveform is a faithful port of the PteronautOS oscillator — not a sine.

## The oscillator

An `OscillatorState` advances a debt-pendulum phase whose `phaseOffset` is attracted to whole strokes by `-ω0² · sin(φ)`. It beat-locks to whole flapping cycles, so cadence and phasing stay coherent under load.

## The shape

`shapeWave` produces an **asymmetric dwell/pointed wave**: per-half ferocity (0…8) sets how much of each half-stroke is dwell versus thrust. A centre-skew parameter shifts the point of reversal. The result is the hard down-stroke and soft recovery of a real wingbeat.

## Ferocity

Ferocity is the texture of the stroke — low values are languid and elastic, high values are sharp and brutal. Tune it to match the animal you are building.
ctl_markdown:
Control runs through the same path as real firmware.

## Channels

CRSF channels arrive raw (172…1811). Aileron, elevator, throttle, rudder, arm, frequency and profile are normalised and fed to the mixer.

## Flapping hysteresis

Flapping engages when throttle exceeds the threshold and releases only after it drops by a hysteresis band — so the wing does not chatter at the edge of idle.

## Steering

Aileron command becomes an asymmetric stroke; elevator becomes tail deflection; rudder shifts the flap amplitude left versus right. Gliding keeps full wing authority.

## Mixer and PID

The ONDAS servo mixer and PID loops are ported from the firmware, so in-simulator behaviour tracks the hardware it mirrors.
tut_lead: From first flap to manual tune.
ff_markdown:
An ornithopter wants to fall. Your job is to convince it otherwise.

## Launch

Rest on the ground, hold **Space** for a hand launch — 8.5 m/s forward, a touch upward. The launch cannot repeat mid-air; commit.

## Flap and glide

Hold **W** for continuous flapping at cruise effort. **Shift + W** demands the full stroke. Release to glide — airspeed and height are spent, never free.

## Turn and climb

**A / D** banks you. **Up / Down** raises and lowers the nose — pulling up costs airspeed, so trade speed for height like the wing you are flying.

## Land

Slow down, keep the nose up, and let the ground meet you gently. **R** resets body and firmware state.
wd_markdown:
Every number you change is a decision the air will judge.

## Chord

A long armwing chord and a tapered handwing give lift inboard and agility outboard. Flatten the tip and you lose roll authority; fatten it and you drag.

## Sweep and washout

Sweep is the slope of the leading edge — it steers crossflow toward the tip. Washout (incidence dropping toward the tip) keeps the tip flying after the root stalls. Both are emergent, not decorative.

## Camber and reflex

Camber buys lift and shifts the zero-lift angle. Trailing-edge reflex shifts the pitching moment — a tail that trims without a tail.

## Stiffness

A stiff armwing and a flexible handwing load-bend into washout. Too stiff and it is a plank; too soft and it folds. Structure is a flight parameter, not a detail.
tune_lead: Dial the wing to your hands.
tune_markdown:
Tuning is the martial art of the simulator — small movements, felt consequences.

## Cadence

Throttle maps to stroke cadence (0.5…3.2 Hz) through the beat-locked oscillator. Find the cadence where the wing stops fighting itself.

## Ferocity

Raise per-half ferocity for a sharper, more brutal stroke; lower it for a languid, elastic one. The wing's character changes before its lift does.

## Mixer and PID

The mixer routes aileron into stroke asymmetry and elevator into tail deflection. PID holds attitude — but every gain is a commitment. Assists are controllers, always visible, always off-able.

## Structure

Bend and twist relax toward their loaded shapes. Tune EI and GJ until the wing carries its own washout. The machine should feel alive under your thumbs, not bolted down.
support_lead: Free as air, kept aloft by hearts.
support_body: BORN2FLAP is free and open source, and it stays that way because of people like you. Every tip and sponsor fuels the next model, the next physics refinement, the next release.
game_valley_desc: A forested valley with a winding river, firs, grass and moss — terrain and tree trunks you can actually collide with.
game_rc_desc: Plug in your own USB transmitter and fly on real sticks — no drivers, no translation layer. F3 opens calibration.
